hand_proof_obligations.proof: For v=3,m=7, width=2 and bit_length(m)=3. The raw length is 6+2*2+2*3+3*7*(2+1)=79, so the frozen even encoder appends one zero and produces length 80=2*40.

MAGIC has 8 bits, gamma(3)=011 has 3, and gamma(7)=00111 has 5, so the header has length 16. Each literal token has 3 bits. The half split at bit 40 is therefore exactly after 8 literal tokens: 16+8*3=40. The suffix is the remaining 13 literal tokens followed by the unique zero pad. Direct concatenation gives 1100101100010110101010101010101010101010.

Every listed variable index is in {1,2,3}, so encode_formula accepts the word as canonical. The first clause (x1 OR x1 OR x1) forces x1=true while the second clause (not x1 OR not x1 OR not x1) forces x1=false. Hence the entire seven-clause conjunction is UNSAT independently of the remaining clauses. Therefore 1||suffix_40 belongs to H_40.

For v=1,m=11, width=1 and bit_length(m)=4. The raw length is 6+2*1+2*4+3*11*(1+1)=82, already even. MAGIC||gamma(1)||gamma(11)=11100101||1||0001011 has length 16. Choosing every literal as positive x1 gives 33 canonical tokens 01, so a canonical length-82 word exists and its first 41 bits are exactly the displayed prefix.

Prepending 1 to the displayed parent suffix gives 11100101100010110101010101010101010101010. The displayed canonical current prefix is bit-for-bit the same 41-bit string. Thus the exact C050 synchronized-language condition has a witness.

This certificate proves only H_40 intersection P_41 nonempty for the unchanged canonical grammar/equal split/swapped interface. It does not prove cover-number growth, a recurrence, circuit lower bounds, or P != NP.
